method.accuracy: Word and character error rate against the script, pooled over every speaker. Both sides are lower-cased, punctuation removed, contractions expanded, numbers written as digits and British spellings made American. Output markup (Qwen3-ASR language tags, VibeVoice speaker labels) is removed first. Speakers' own slips count against every model alike.
method.isolation: One model at a time. The run refuses to start a model while any other engine process is alive, and confirms the model's server has exited before the next starts.
method.latencyTarget: 1000 ms from the end of an utterance to its final text.
method.runs: One pass per model per recording.
method.score: A 0–100 score from fixed scales, so it doesn't change when other models are added: accuracy (60%: 15% word errors scores 0, 2% scores 100), typical wait (25%: 1.5 s scores 0, 50 ms scores 100) and slow wait, the slowest 1 in 10 (15%: 3 s scores 0, 150 ms scores 100), each on a log scale so every halving counts the same.
method.settings: Each engine with its defaults, except thinking: models on llama-server run with thinking off (--reasoning off), the same as in Toolbench. The only other arguments are the model files and a port. CrispASR also gets --auto-download, so it may fetch helper files its defaults use; CrispASR and the Python runner have no thinking to turn off.
method.streamingModels: Each recording played into /v1/realtime at real speed in 80 ms blocks; an utterance's words are those arriving before the next utterance starts (at most 5 s after it ends); latency is from its end to its last word.
method.wholeUtteranceModels: Each utterance sent alone to POST /v1/audio/transcriptions as soon as it ends; latency is the request time. One utterance is sent untimed first to warm the model up.
